title: Neighbors' review requests and repeated delay, 2022-2026 against 2019-2022
question: How often did the Planning Commission take discretionary review after August 2022, and how often were projects put off again and again?
finding: The 2022-08 to 2026-07 minutes hold 127 discretionary-review cases: 93 were decided and review was taken in 38 (40.9%, against 56.1% in 2019-01 to 2022-08), with the permit refused in 0; 29 were withdrawn and 5 were only continued in these files. Of 742 projects at an address, 22.0% were continued at least once (0.44 continuances per project, against 0.65 before) and 38 were continued three or more times.
how: A review case is one case number with the suffix DRP (requested by a neighbor) or DRM (mandatory); its outcome is the most decisive action on it: refused (disapproved), review taken (took discretionary review, or approved with changes), not taken, withdrawn, or only continued. A project is one case-number root at an address; a continuance is a hearing date on which any of its items was continued. Same rules as the “votes” analysis for 2019-2022.
limits: The minutes do not say who asked for a review; requesters are private people and are not named or counted here. A continuance can be asked for by the applicant, the neighbor or staff, and a case decided after July 2026 or before August 2022 shows here as "only continued". Mandatory review cases (DRM) are included in both periods.

sources.t: San Francisco Planning: Planning Commission and Historic Preservation Commission minutes, August 2022 to July 2026 (hearing archive; saved by hand 20 Nov 2026)
